subject: Azure private offer: commit mapping and reseller vs distributor split
messages:
From: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@opal-systems.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 14 May 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Azure private offer questions on distributor/reseller splits

Hi Irene,

Thanks again for the walkthrough earlier. We're excited about moving the Azure private offer forward, but we need to understand two operational items before we can sign:

1) How do you recommend we map our multi-year commit to the Azure SKU buckets? We have a mix of reserved and metered usage and want predictable list-price anchoring for year 1.
2) Our preferred reseller (DistCo) insists on an 8% distributor uplift on list price to cover VAT and local invoicing — can Redwood support that pass-through or do you require a single net price to be listed in the private offer?

If you can share a simple proforma (line items + recommended list-price anchors) and the invoicing flow (who issues the invoice to us and who pays DistCo), that would help speed procurement.

Appreciate it —
Sarah Liu
Head of Cloud Procurement
Opal Systems

---
Attachment: Opal_usage_sample.csv (stub)

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@opal-systems.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 14 May 2026 17:06:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Azure private offer questions on distributor/reseller splits

Hi Sarah —

Thanks for the clear list. High level answers first, then we'll follow up with a proforma and commit mapping: 

- Commit mapping: we recommend anchoring the private-offer list price to a conservative SKU bucket that matches your predominant VM/GPU usage. We'll send a CSV with the recommended mapping (month-by-month). That mapping supports tiered price buckets so the private offer lists the per-unit list price and then the private-offer discount is applied at checkout.

- Reseller/distributor uplift: Azure marketplace requires a single private-offer price; channel uplifts are typically handled off-market (reseller invoices). Practically: Redwood can publish the private offer at the agreed net list price, and DistCo can invoice Opal for their uplift separately. The main friction is tax and invoice timing — we can support distributor pass-through if DistCo provides a signed reseller agreement and you confirm the VAT handling.

I've looped in Ben and Karthik to provide the proforma and an initial margin waterfall we typically use. Ben — can you attach a proforma and a sample commit mapping? Karthik — any concerns on billing/invoicing or tax we should flag?

Best,
Irene
Senior Commercial Ops
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 14 May 2026 19:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Azure private offer questions on distributor/reseller splits

Irene / Sarah —

Attached are two docs: offer_proforma_Opal_AZ.xlsx and commit_mapping_v1.csv (stubs attached). Quick notes from our side: 

- Recommended structure (year 1): list-price per unit = $0.120/token-equivalent for ModelX (anchored to SKU bucket AZ-M-Large); private-offer discount = 25% (customer-facing price).
- Reseller/distributor splits (example waterfall):
  * Gross list: $100k
  * Private-offer discount (25%): -$25k
  * Net to Redwood: $75k
  * Reseller commission (if via Redwood-managed reseller program): 10% of net ($7.5k)
  * Distributor uplift (off-market invoice to customer): DistCo requested 8% on gross list ($8k) — this is paid separately by Opal to DistCo.

- Important: Azure will only show the private-offer price (post-discount) on the marketplace. Any distributor uplift has to be invoiced off-market. If Opal requires a single invoice that includes DistCo fees, we need DistCo to be billing Opal directly and provide tax documentation.

- Attachments: the proforma has a line-by-line SKU map and an example DocuSign-friendly PO template. The CSV shows monthly commit smoothing so you don't hit large bumps in metered months.

Next steps I suggest:
1) Opal confirms acceptance of the sample mapping (or marks changes in the CSV).
2) DistCo signs reseller addendum (I attached a redline they can edit and return).
3) We prepare the final private-offer payload for Azure and share a DocuSign link for Opal to sign.

--
Ben Carter
Senior Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments: offer_proforma_Opal_AZ.xlsx (spreadsheet), commit_mapping_v1.csv (csv)

From: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@distco.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@opal-systems.com>
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Azure private offer questions on distributor/reseller splits

Ben / Irene,

Thanks for the breakdown. A couple of operational items from the distributor side: 

- VAT & invoice timing: Opal is in the EU and expects DistCo to handle VAT. For us to absorb that, we need the uplift to be calculated on the gross list (not post-discount). The 8% uplift we asked for covers VAT and local remittance overhead.
- Single-invoice ask: Opal prefers a single invoice that shows both the Azure private-offer charge and the DistCo uplift. If Redwood cannot facilitate a consolidated invoice (since Azure handles the private-offer billing), we will need a mechanism to reference the Azure invoice ID so we can reconcile.

Can Redwood confirm whether Azure private-offer payload can include a buyer reference field (invoice reference) that DistCo can use for reconciliation? Also, can you confirm timeline to publish once DocuSign is signed? We need this live before June 1 to align with Opal's quarter close.

Regards,
Tom Reynolds
Head of Channel Sales
DistCo (Distributor)

Attachment: distco_terms_redline.pdf (redline)

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2026 11:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Azure private offer questions on distributor/reseller splits - internal notes

Irene / Ben,

Internal note on the buyer reference: Azure private-offer payload supports an optional buyerReference string which will be echoed in the invoice metadata from Microsoft. We can populate that with the Opal PO# and DistCo uplift reference. Two caveats:
1) The buyerReference is limited to 64 characters and is not a substitute for legal invoicing.
2) The Azure invoice will still be generated by Microsoft; DistCo must invoice Opal separately.

Timeline: once DocuSign is signed and DistCo returns the reseller addendum (we have the redline), we can submit to Azure; publishing typically takes 24-72 hours for validation. That gets us comfortably before June 1 if signatures are returned by Friday, May 22.

I'll attach a snippet for the buyerReference format we recommend.

-Naomi
Legal & Pricing Ops
Redwood Inference
